note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment planning following confirmed ISUP grade group 3 prostate cancer with rising PSA.

Recently retired freelance translator with a history of osteoarthritis and benign prostatic hyperplasia. The patient reports a gradual increase in PSA levels over the past two years, from 11.5 ng/mL in June 2023 to 16.5 ng/mL in February 2025, with a corresponding rise in IPSS score to 16/35. He has been managed with tamsulosin for LUTS and paracetamol as needed for joint pain. Socially, he lives alone but maintains close contact with his adult daughter, who serves as his primary next-of-kin. He drinks approximately two units of alcohol per week and walks 20 minutes daily. Recent dermatology appointment for actinic keratosis check was unremarkable. He has previously declined participation in research studies, including active surveillance trials.

Per rectum, the prostate feels symmetrically enlarged without palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals mild bilateral knee crepitus and no lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses. Vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 147/74 mmHg and heart rate of 70 bpm.
